description: Full-text search over received and sent mail (subject, body and addresses), newest first; every word must match. Narrows by agent, sender, recipient, date range, attachment, folder, label or direction. Each hit says whether it was `received` or `sent` and carries a snippet around the match.

after.description: Only mail at or after this time (ISO 8601, or YYYY-MM-DD).

agent_id.description: Filter by agent id or name. A key tied to one agent always reads that agent's mail, and naming another agent is a 403.

assignee.description: Only mail in threads assigned to this member (an email or a user id `usr_…`), `none` for threads assigned to nobody, `any` for threads assigned to someone. `me` is the person signed in, in the dashboard or through an app connected by sign-in; a plain API key has no person behind it, so `me` from one is a 422.

before.description: Only mail before this time (ISO 8601, or YYYY-MM-DD).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's `next_cursor`.

folder.description: Which folder's mail to return, or `all` for every folder. Without it: every folder except trash.

from.description: The sender's address contains this text (the display name, which the sender chooses, is not matched).

has_attachment.description: `true` for mail with a file attachment, `false` for mail without.

label.description: Only mail in threads carrying this label (a name, or a label id `lbl_…`).

q.description: Full-text search: every word must appear in the subject, body or addresses, as a whole word or, from three letters up, the start of one (`inv` finds `invoice`). At most 16 different words (more is a 400). It also takes operators, each narrowing the search as the query parameter of the same name does: `from:` and `to:` (an address or part of one), `label:` (a name; one with spaces in quotes, `label:"Needs reply"`), `in:` (a folder, or `all`), `after:` and `before:` (a date or ISO 8601 time), `has:attachment`, `is:read`, `is:unread`, `is:assigned`, `is:unassigned` and `assignee:` (a member's email or `usr_…` id, or `me`, the person signed in: from a plain API key, which has no person behind it, `me` is a 422). An operator given a value it cannot take is a 400 that says what it takes.

read.description: `false` for mail in unread threads only, `true` for mail in read ones (`is:unread` and `is:read` in `q`).

to.description: A recipient address contains this text.

type.description: Only received or only sent mail.

name: mails_search_mail
title: Search mail
